name: Password Hashing Assessment
description: Assessment of password hashing implementations including Argon2, bcrypt, scrypt, and PBKDF2. Covers work factor evaluation, salt generation and storage, algorithm selection review, and identification of insecure password storage patterns (plain text, unsalted hashes, fast hashes).

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to password hashing assessment

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands why specialised password hashing functions are needed
evidence: Can explain why SHA-256 is unsuitable for password hashing
Understands the role of salting and work factors in password hashing
Can name recommended password hashing functions (Argon2, bcrypt, scrypt)

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Identifies password hashing schemes and basic weaknesses under supervision
evidence: Identifies password hashing algorithms from stored hash formats (bcrypt prefix, Argon2 encoding)
Detects unsalted or fast-hash password storage in code review under guidance
Uses hashcat or John the Ripper to test password hash strength on lab data
Documents password hashing findings following lab templates

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses password hashing implementations and work factor adequacy
evidence: Evaluates Argon2 parameter selection (memory, iterations, parallelism) against current guidance (RFC 9106, OWASP)
Assesses bcrypt/scrypt work factors relative to current hardware capabilities
Identifies PBKDF2 with insufficient iterations or weak PRF selection
Produces actionable findings with specific parameter recommendations referencing OWASP, NIST SP 800-63B-4, or SP 800-132

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Handles complex password storage assessments; benchmarks cracking resistance
evidence: Benchmarks password hash cracking rates on current GPU hardware to validate work factors
Evaluates custom password hashing constructions for design weaknesses
Assesses password hashing in federated identity and credential storage systems
Reviews and mentors junior staff on password hashing assessment

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines password hashing assessment methodology; recognised authority on credential storage
evidence: Authored or maintains the lab's password hashing assessment methodology and parameter recommendations
Published research on password cracking techniques or hash function resistance
Provides expert guidance on password hashing migration strategies
Trains teams on password hashing internals, attacks, and hardware-aware parameter selection

assessment_methods.description: Audit a credential storage system: identify the hashing algorithm, evaluate parameters, and estimate cracking resistance on current hardware
Review password hashing assessment findings from a recent engagement for completeness and accuracy of parameter recommendations
